excludedAssessments.summary: The private-message specialization, 30-row algebraic equivalence, input-only product marginalization, extended-real inequalities, Q0 midpoint dependence, and finiteness of V_0 are established conditional on the structured transcription. However, the checker does not establish the claimed render-complete visible-glyph semantic equivalence to the official PDF, so the composite source-fidelity claim remains unresolved.
scopeQualifications: The correctness of Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 is taken as a primary-source premise and is not independently reproved.
Setting R0=0, expanding each minimum into scalar branches, and splitting interval constraints yields exactly 30 rows: 26 branch rows and 4 interval rows.
The local and transcribed rows agree modulo the identities I(U,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(U;A|W) and I(V,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(V;A|W).

Product input-only marginalization preserves all audited single-output terms and side conditions because the term list contains neither joint (G,K) terms nor conditioning of one receiver output on another; reverse inclusion is immediate.
With sup(empty set)=-infinity, feasible-set restriction and q=1/2 membership establish V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K).
For Q0={0,1/2,1}, endpoint mutual informations vanish, so every audited row depends on the receiver channels only through midpoint values (c,g,k,c).
The Q0-supported feasible set is nonempty, and branch-zero bounds give 0 <= V_0(g,k) <= 2; thus V_0 is finite and unambiguous for realizable g,k.
evidenceIssues: The terminal attestation proves successful execution and checker acceptance, including PDF authentication, structural and geometry checks, extracted-character comparison, all 30 generated-row comparisons, and the single-output term whitelist.
The Type1 handling inventories CharString names and binds whole-font bytes by hashes but does not parse or execute Type1 CharString programs to verify the actually painted glyph outlines.

ToUnicode mappings, glyph names, widths, declared bounding boxes, CharStrings-dictionary membership, and hard-coded font hashes do not independently establish that visible glyph shapes have the asserted Unicode semantics.

Accordingly, successful checker acceptance does not prove the stronger claimed render-complete semantic equivalence; because source fidelity is a conjunct of the declared composite claim, the conditional correctness of the later mathematics is insufficient for a valid verdict.
